baseline.versionPolicy: Stable outcomes apply across supported releases; verify runtime, toolchain, module, security, and standard-library details against the repository-selected Go version.

owns: HTTP, RPC, CLI, or message mapping

hardOutcomes: Business facts, shared state, and goroutines have explicit owners.
Framework and infrastructure choices do not define the core dependency direction.
Package imports are acyclic and runtime call graphs terminate safely.

invariants.outcome: Package imports are acyclic, synchronous calls terminate safely, and every authoritative fact, shared state value, and background goroutine has an explicit owner.
invariants.equivalenceCriteria: Any package layout and injection mechanism qualify when import evidence, mutation paths, and shutdown tests prove the same result.

invariants.outcome: Actual Context chains, goroutines, connections, commands, servers, and workers propagate cancellation and deadlines and have bounded admission, panic handling, waiting, and shutdown semantics.
invariants.equivalenceCriteria: Explicit lifecycle coordinators or framework hooks qualify when leak, panic, cancellation, saturation, and termination evidence cover owned work.

invariants.outcome: Every adopted HTTP, RPC, CLI, message, file, path, unsafe, cgo, identity, tenant, secret, diagnostic, limit, and public-error boundary is explicit, least-privilege, and negatively testable.
invariants.equivalenceCriteria: Alternative routers, codecs, middleware, and policy engines comply when negative tests prove equivalent validation, authorization, resource bounds, and non-disclosure.

invariants.outcome: Every adopted transaction, migration, message, cache, remote call, retry, and cross-resource write preserves required consistency under duplicate delivery, timeout, and partial failure.
invariants.equivalenceCriteria: Any persistence and delivery mechanisms qualify when fault tests prove transaction ownership, safe retry or deduplication, and compatible schema evolution.

invariants.outcome: Entrypoints, configuration, toolchain, dependencies, generated inputs, tests, and release artifacts are determinable and reproducible from a clean checkout.
invariants.equivalenceCriteria: Single- or multi-module repositories comply when locked toolchain and repository commands build and validate the actual shipped entries without machine-specific state.

proves: All selected packages and commands compile for the active build target.
doesNotProve: Other target platforms, runtime configuration, or failure paths are correct.

proves: Exercised supported paths do not trigger the Go race detector.
doesNotProve: Unexercised schedules are race-free or higher-level consistency is correct.

proves: Repository package tests pass for the active toolchain and exercised behavior.
doesNotProve: Untested production integrations, targets, and failure modes satisfy invariants.

proves: The active vet analyzers report no findings in selected packages.
doesNotProve: The design is secure, race-free, or behaviorally correct.

scenarios.failure: A write commits before acknowledgement fails, and a retry repeats a non-idempotent mutation or external side effect.
scenarios.requiredOutcome: Inject failure at transaction and acknowledgement boundaries and prove idempotency, deduplication, outbox, or an equivalent conflict protocol.

scenarios.failure: Cancellation is dropped or dependencies close before owned goroutines drain, causing leaks, hung shutdown, or writes through closed resources.
scenarios.requiredOutcome: Exercise signal-driven shutdown under in-flight load, stop admission, propagate context, wait with a bound, and close resources in dependency order.
